Headquarters: US - Remote

Wrike is the most powerful work management platform. Built for teams and organizations looking to collaborate, create, and exceed every day, Wrike brings everyone and all work into a single place to remove complexity, increase productivity, and free people up to focus on their most purposeful work.

Wrike is our people, not a place. As a distributed team, we own our growth, stay globally connected, and rely on the product we build to deliver impactful work alongside brilliant minds. You'll have real ownership over meaningful work, a global team that has your back, and the flexibility to do your best work your way. If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

Our vision:  A world where everyone is free to focus on their most purposeful work, together. 

About the Role:

You'll own your outcomes, from the strategies you run to the conversations that shape what we build next. We're looking for a results-oriented Demand Marketing Manager with proven B2B SaaS experience to lead one of Wrike's flagship global integrated campaigns. These campaigns bring together product, industry and buyer-journey strategy into a coordinated program that generates pipeline, accelerates deals and drives expansion across our customer base.

This is a hybrid role: part campaign leader, part hands-on practitioner. You'll own the campaign strategy, plan, budget and results. You'll also directly execute sponsored media and email/nurture programs. At the same time, you'll orchestrate the work of partner teams, including digital, ABM, field and events, and webinars, and make sure it all stays aligned with campaign goals and messaging.

You'll partner closely with product marketing, customer marketing, content, digital, field and regional marketing, ABM, sales development, and marketing operations. The ideal candidate has managed complex, multi-region campaigns, thrives in a metrics-driven environment, and uses Wrike to run their own work.

Your Impact:

• Campaign Strategy & Planning

• Own the integrated campaign brief, strategy and roadmap, aligned to company priorities, product launches, target industries and personas, and buyer journeys.

• Define the approach for both new-customer acquisition (Land) and existing-customer growth (Expand), including audiences, messaging and channel mix for each.

• Translate positioning from product marketing into campaign themes and use-case-led messaging that resonates with enterprise buying committees.

• Manage the campaign budget, allocating investment across channels and adjusting based on performance.

• Execution (Hands-On)

• Plan, launch and optimize sponsored media programs, including content syndication (including regional and local-language placements), sponsored webinars and virtual events, podcast sponsorships, and industry publication newsletter or dedicated email placements.

• Select and manage third-party media and event vendors, negotiate placements within budget, and track delivery and results.

• Build and manage email, nurture and lifecycle programs for prospects and existing customers, including customer newsletters and workflow- or role-based nurture streams.

• Brief creative and content teams, and manage production and launch of the assets each tactic needs.

• Monitor performance, run tests and optimize against targets for actions, MQLs, meetings and pipeline.

• Program Oversight & Cross-Functional Leadership

• Oversee the programs run by partner teams, including paid digital (managed by the digital team), ABM (1:1 and 1:few), events (field, executive and customer events), and Wrike-hosted webinars and "deminars", and keep them aligned to campaign strategy, messaging, timelines and goals.

• Integrate those programs with sponsored media and nurture into one coherent buyer journey, including follow-up and sales handoff.

• Work with sales and sales development to ensure campaign assets, plays and follow-up cadences support target accounts and pipeline goals.

• Balance global strategy with regional relevance, including localization, regional events and partner activity, across EMEA, the Americas and APJ.

• Workflow & Operations

• Run campaign planning in Wrike, including briefs, templates, dependencies, workback schedules and creative requests, to keep a large cross-functional program visible and on track.

• Work with marketing operations to build, QA and track programs across tools such as Marketo, Salesforce, 6sense and Tableau.

• Identify risks, resolve conflicts and escalate when needed to keep the program on schedule.

• Measurement & Optimization

• Define campaign KPIs across target-account coverage, engagement, intent, actions/MQLs, meetings, pipeline and revenue, including both sourced and influenced contribution.

• Establish baselines and measure impact on target accounts, then use the data to recommend and drive optimizations.

• Report regularly to senior leadership through dashboards, presentations and Wrike updates.

Your Qualifications:

• 5–7 years of experience in B2B SaaS demand generation or integrated campaign roles, including leading large, multi-channel or multi-region programs.

• Hands-on experience executing sponsored media, content syndication and email/nurture programs.

• Experience leading both acquisition and expansion campaigns, with exposure to ABM.

• Demonstrated ability to align many workstreams and stakeholders across digital, events, webinars, ABM and sales outreach, including programs you don't directly own.

• Experience owning or managing a program budget and working with third-party vendors.

• Hands-on experience with work management tools (preferably Wrike) for campaign planning and collaboration.

• Familiarity with marketing automation, CRM and ABM tools such as Marketo, Salesforce, Tableau, 6sense or Sendoso.

• Strong project management skills, attention to detail and a data-driven mindset.

• Comfort working across time zones with global teams.

• Preferred Qualifications

• Experience marketing to complex enterprise or industry-specific buyers, such as manufacturing.

• Ownership of campaign workstreams in Wrike, including templates, dependencies and reporting.

• Experience coordinating localized campaigns, regional events and partner co-marketing.

• Understanding of enterprise SaaS buyer journeys and content strategies that support multi-stakeholder decisions.

Our Work Style:

• A high-impact role on a high-performing demand generation team.

• A collaborative team culture that values initiative and innovation.

• Opportunity to make a direct contribution to revenue growth and brand visibility.

• Competitive salary, full benefits, and flexible working environment.

About the role

We're hiring two backend-heavy full-stack engineers (SDE 2 or SDE 3) for the Cowork team at Sarvam. Cowork is the agentic side of Indus: users hand it real work, and an agent plans, uses tools and connectors, works in a cloud sandbox, and hands back files, docs and artifacts across web, Android, iOS, macOS and Windows.

The role is full stack, but the centre of gravity is the backend: the BFF that every client talks to, and increasingly the agent harness behind it. You'll ship features end to end, from the API and data model through to the client screens on mobile, desktop and web.

What you'll work on

Most of your time goes into the BFF and the services around it; the rest into client work and the harness, depending on what the roadmap needs that quarter.
• 
BFF (Chat Service): design and own the APIs that web, mobile and desktop share: sessions, conversations, streaming turns, artifacts, connectors, custom and managed agents. Data modelling, migrations, auth and RBAC, pagination and search.
• 
Real-time streaming: stream LLM output, tool calls and agent events from the harness to clients over an event bus, and keep it correct under reconnects, retries and partial failures.
• 
Agent harness and platform: contribute to Panja, our agent harness: tool and MCP integrations, sandboxed execution, file and artifact flows, latency and token-cost work.
• 
Clients: build features end to end on our Kotlin/Compose Multiplatform apps (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows) and the Next.js web app, so a feature you design in the backend reaches users on every surface.
• 
Production ownership: observability, on-call, RCAs, and making the system faster and cheaper with numbers to back it.

Tech stack

Python and PostgreSQL are the core; you don't need every item below on day one.
• 
Backend: Python, SQLAlchemy + Alembic, PostgreSQL, OpenAPI
• 
Supporting services: Go
• 
Mobile and desktop: Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows)
• 
Web: Next.js, React, TypeScript

What we're looking for

A strong backend engineer who has also shipped real frontend work and is happy to keep doing both.
• 
3+ years (SDE 2) or 5+ years (SDE 3) building and running production backend services.
• 
Deep in at least one backend language; Python preferred, Go, Kotlin/JVM or TypeScript/Node also welcome.
• 
Solid API and data-model design: REST/streaming APIs, PostgreSQL schema design, migrations, indexing, transactions.
• 
Distributed-systems fundamentals: async processing, queues or event streams, idempotency, retries, failure handling.
• 
Production experience on Kubernetes or a similar platform, with observability you actually used to debug an incident.
• 
Has shipped user-facing features on at least one client platform: Android, iOS, desktop or web (React/Next.js). Kotlin/Compose experience is a plus, not a gate.
• 
Willing to pick up the side of the stack they know less, and to learn agent and LLM systems on the job.
• 
Clear written communication: design docs, PR descriptions, RCAs.
Nice to have
• 
Built on LLM APIs: tool calling, streaming, prompt caching, evals, or an agent loop of your own.
• 
MCP servers or clients, OAuth connector integrations, or sandboxed code execution.
• 
Kotlin Multiplatform / Compose Multiplatform, or native Android/iOS.
• 
Real-time systems: WebSockets/SSE, NATS, Kafka, or Temporal-style durable workflows.
• 
Go services, or performance and cost work with measurable before/after numbers.
• 
Open-source work or public writing we can read.

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and related services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all outdoor home services - pest control, pool cleaning, window cleaning, and more.

About Engineering at LawnStarter

Our engineering team builds the platform that connects hundreds of thousands of homeowners with over 70,000 active service pros. Engineering here is fast - we ship constantly, we own our systems end-to-end, and we don't tolerate "not my problem." - AI-forward is not a buzzword here - we expect you to lead your team on how to use it, not just follow along

- Cross-functional partnership: You're the interface between your team and Product, Design, and other engineering teams. Decisions get made, not stalled.

- AI adoption: You're actively introducing AI tools and workflows into how your team operates - code review, documentation, sprint planning, debugging. You set the pace, not follow it.

Building people leadership depth as the team scales

LawnStarter is expanding into new service verticals quickly. That means new headcount, new complexity, and more pressure on EMs to develop the next generation of senior engineers and tech leads - not just ship features. We need an EM who's done this before, not one who's figuring it out.

Managing distributed teams without losing culture or accountability

Our engineering team spans multiple time zones and countries. Async communication, remote 1:1s, and distributed sprint ceremonies are the norm - not a workaround. An EM who needs daily in-person proximity to lead effectively won't thrive here.

Turning delivery consistency into a competitive advantage

We have product-market fit and real momentum. The constraint now is shipping reliably enough to compound on that momentum. Your team's velocity and predictability directly affects LawnStarter's ability to launch new services and capture market share.

We need an EM who can hold business value and technical soundness in view at once and make the tradeoff calls - not one who stalls when Product wants speed, Security wants rigor, and Architecture wants the durable answer.

Turning AI adoption into throughput without sacrificing craftsmanship

We're not experimenting with AI on the margins. Claude Code, spec-driven development, and AI-assisted review are becoming default workflows here - and we track adoption seriously. We need an EM who can turn "the team uses AI" into measurable throughput without letting quality slip, with real opinions about where AI helps and where it quietly creates debt.

- Underperformance is addressed directly and documented, not deferred
